---
title: "Data Modeling: Interpolation and Curve-Fitting"
engine: julia
---

This chapter deals with modeling discrete one-dimensional data with functions.

Tabular data has a discrete nature, therefore not allowing continuous
operations---such as continuous evaluations, derivation, integration, etc.---to
find maxima, minima, areas, and the like. Modeling tabular data allows one to
obtain a surrogate continuous function for the original tabular data.

One can identify two main approaches in constructing such a function: (i) one
that passes through all of the tabulated data points, i.e., an _interpolation_,
and (ii) one that captures the data behavior within a pre-defined funcion base,
i.e., _curve-fitting_.

### Least-Squares

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
#| message: false

using Random
using Plots
gr()

function tmp_gen_lsq(; rnd = 0.25)
    __X = rand(15) * 6 .+ 1.0
    RND = rnd * rand(length(__X))
    CST = 10.0 + rand() * 5
    __Y = sin.(__X .- 1.0) + 0.5 * __X .+ CST + RND
    return (__X, __Y)
end

data = tmp_gen_lsq()

MODELS = Dict(
    :quadr => [
        x -> one(x),
        x -> x,
        x -> x^2,
    ],
    :cubic => [
        x -> one(x),
        x -> x,
        x -> x^2,
        x -> x^3,
    ],
)

function leastSq(the_x, the_y, MODEL)
    X = hcat([ F.(the_x) for F in MODEL ]...)
    y = copy(the_y)
    return a = X \ y
end

model(MOD, a, x) = sum(a .* [F.(x) for F in MOD])
```

Suppose one has tabular data from an experiment that relates a system performace
parameter, say, $y$, to input parameter $x$ values, as shown:

```{julia}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2
scatter(data...,
    xlabel="\$x\$",
    ylabel="\$y\$",
    label="data",
    legend=:topright,
    size=(480, 240),
)
```

The available data is limited, taken at irregular intervals, and contains
uncertainty. A designer of a new system or product of performance $y$ may need
performace values for arbitrary $x$ values. Moreover, the designer may need
information about local maxima, minima for $y$, and the corresponding $x$
values. Raw tabular data offer challenges to all these very applicable tasks.
